_metadata.source: USGS-NASA Planetary Geologic Mapping Program & Astropedia
_metadata.map_reference: Geologic Map of Mars, USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3292 (Tanaka et al., 2014)
_metadata.description: Standardized geologic units, surface rock formations, and chemical weathering hazards of Mars.

geologic_epochs.characteristics: Heavy meteorite bombardment, liquid surface water, phyllosilicate (clay) formation, neutral-to-alkaline pH

predominant_units.name: Late Noachian Highland Unit
predominant_units.lithology: Valley network terminal deltas, layered sediments

geologic_epochs.characteristics: Widespread flood volcanism, catastrophic mega-outflow channels, sulfuric acid weathering, sulfate deposit formation

predominant_units.name: Late Hesperian Lowland Unit
predominant_units.lithology: Outflow channel sediments, sulfate evaporite beds

geologic_epochs.characteristics: Hyper-arid cold desert, eolian erosion, perchlorate-rich dust accumulation, active dust storms, polar ice cap layering

predominant_units.name: Early Amazonian Volcanic Unit
predominant_units.lithology: Tharsis Montes and Olympus Mons basalt flows

predominant_units.name: Late Amazonian Polar and Eolian Dunes
predominant_units.lithology: Active transverse sand dunes, water-ice/CO2 ice blankets
predominant_units.roughness: High entrapment hazard (soft sand, wheel sinkage)

acidic_sulfate_enrichment_regions.region_name: Vera Rubin Ridge & Sulfate Unit (Gale Crater)

acidic_sulfate_enrichment_regions.acidity_level: High acidity groundwaters (pH ~2 to 4 in ancient era)
acidic_sulfate_enrichment_regions.corrosion_hazard_for_rover: Low modern atmospheric corrosion; high soil salinity

perchlorate_soil_concentrations.impact_on_exploration: Strong oxidizer; toxic to human tissue; lowers freezing point of water to create transient brines.
